chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus ibn Yaqoub, who said:

When Abu Al-Hasan Musa (peace be upon him) returned from Baghdad and proceeded to Al-Madina, his daughter died in Faid. So he buried her and ordered one of his slaves to apply plaster to her grave, write her name on a tablet, and place it in the grave.

key_terms.يُجَصِّصَ: To apply plaster or clay (jass) to a surface, specifically a grave

ai.seo_question: What is the jurisprudential basis for plastering graves and placing name tablets in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: This narration from *Al-Kafi* establishes the Sunnah of the Imams regarding grave markers, specifically noting that Imam Musa al-Kadhim (AS) ordered his slave to plaster the grave and place a tablet with his daughter's name inside. This practice underscores the Shia jurisprudential distinction between permissible identification and the prohibition of excessive veneration or idolatry associated with later customs. It serves as a primary textual basis for the permissibility of *jass* (plastering) and *khatm* (sealing) in Shia fiqh.

en.hubeali: A number of our companions, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ibn Mahboub, from Yunus Bin Yaqoub who said,

‘When Abu Al Hassan Musa<sup>asws</sup> returned from Baghdad and went to Al Medina, and daughter of his<sup>asws</sup> died. So he<sup>asws</sup> buried her and ordered one of his<sup>asws</sup> slaves that he should apply clay on her grave and write her name upon a tombstone, and make it to be in her grave’.
en.sarwar: 3. A number of our people have narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad ibn Mahbub from Yunus ibn Ya’qub who has said the following: “

When abu al-Hassan, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, returned from Baghdad to al-Madinah, one of his daughters died in Fayd. He (the Imam) buried her and commanded certain people of his followers to build her grave with lime, write her name on the tombstone and place it on the grave.”
